method: Public pages rendered and read through CloakBrowser. Browser closed after research. References support the upcoming unique SCI gates, not a separate repeated gate.

references.title: 6.777J/2.751J Material Property Database: Aluminum
references.observed: The Young modulus entry is 70 GPa and cites Thin Solid Films 270 (1995), p.263. This is 7 times 10^10 Pa, not the source textbook's 7 times 10^7 N/m^2. This supports correcting the order of magnitude for the typical aluminum example, not certifying every alloy or temperature.

references.title: Elastic deformation: Hooke's law and stiffness
references.observed: Distinguishes elastic recovery from the proportional stress-strain region. Defines Young and shear modulus separately, and notes direction dependence for anisotropic materials. Used to qualify small-strain Hookean assumptions, not to impose universal material behavior.

references.title: Plastic deformation: strength and ductility
references.observed: The example is a nominal stress-strain curve. Yield, ultimate tensile strength, failure strength and ductility are distinct; the maximum nominal stress marks necking onset. A modern proof-stress convention is not the textbook's historical 0.1% residual-strain definition.

limits: No new dependencies, services, source edits or user-browser interaction. The initial guessed mechanical-testing page returned 404 and was not used as scientific evidence.
